# HeartRateLab: Complete Pipeline Demonstration

This notebook demonstrates the complete HeartRateLab pipeline end-to-end:
1. **Load real HRV data**
2. **Fit mechanistic models with Bayesian inference**
3. **Generate synthetic ensemble**
4. **Visualize uncertainty and dynamics**
5. **Validate statistical fit**

## Setup

```{julia}

using Plots, StatsPlots
using Statistics, Random
using DataFrames

# Set random seed for reproducibility
Random.seed!(42)
```

## Part 4: Model Fitting and Synthetic Generation

### 4.1 The Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (LIF) Cardiac Pacemaker

The **Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (LIF)** model represents the sinoatrial node as a single-compartment
membrane whose voltage $V$ is governed by:

$$\tau \frac{dV}{dt} = -(V - V_\text{rest}) + R \cdot I$$

When $V$ crosses the firing threshold $V_\text{threshold}$, a **spike** (heartbeat) is emitted and
$V$ resets to $V_\text{reset}$. The inter-beat interval (IBI) is the time between consecutive
spikes. DifferentialEquations.jl is used to integrate this ODE with `Tsit5()` and a
`ContinuousCallback` for precise spike detection.

| Parameter | Symbol | Value | Physiological meaning |
|-----------|--------|-------|-----------------------|
| Time constant | $\tau$ | to explore | Sets intrinsic inter-beat timescale |
| Resting potential | $V_\text{rest}$ | −70 mV | Baseline membrane voltage |
| Reset potential | $V_\text{reset}$ | −70 mV | Voltage after spike (equals $V_\text{rest}$) |
| Spike threshold | $V_\text{thr}$ | −40 mV | Threshold that triggers a beat |
| Membrane resistance | $R$ | to explore | Scales input current to voltage units |
| **Input current** | **$I$** | **fitted** | **Sole free parameter — encodes autonomic drive** |

The **nullcline** (steady-state without spikes) satisfies $V^* = V_\text{rest} + R \cdot I$.
For spiking to occur we need $V^* > V_\text{threshold}$, i.e., $R \cdot I > \Delta V$ where
$\Delta V = V_\text{threshold} - V_\text{rest} = 30\,\text{mV}$.

The analytical period is:
$$T = \tau \cdot \ln\!\left(\frac{R I}{R I - \Delta V}\right)$$
and the inverse (desired period $\to$ required $I$):
$$I(T) = \frac{\Delta V}{R\,(1 - e^{-T/\tau})}$$
So once $V_\text{rest}$ and $V_\text{threshold}$ are fixed ($\Delta V = 30\,\text{mV}$), the
product $R \cdot I$ is the only relevant quantity — $R$ sets the scale of $I$ without changing
the dynamics.

```{julia}
# ── LIF physiological parameters (values to explore in this notebook) ───────
τ_lif       = 220.0   # ms  — sets intrinsic inter-beat timescale
V_rest_lif  = -70.0   # mV
V_thr_lif   = -40.0   # mV
V_reset_lif = -70.0   # mV
R_lif       = 20.0    # mV / (current unit)  — scales I to voltage
I_normal    = 1.52    # current; typical starting value to explore

# ── Slope-field grid in (t, V) space ────────────────────────────────────────
V_grid_vals = range(-85.0, -29.5, length = 12)
t_grid_vals = range(0.0, 6 * τ_lif,  length = 20)

T_flat    = vec([t for t in t_grid_vals, v in V_grid_vals])
V_flat    = vec([v for t in t_grid_vals, v in V_grid_vals])
dVdt_flat = vec([(-(v - V_rest_lif) + R_lif * I_normal) / τ_lif
                  for t in t_grid_vals, v in V_grid_vals])

# Normalise arrows so all have the same visual length
arrow_scale = 5.0
norms       = sqrt.(1.0 .+ dVdt_flat .^ 2)
dT_arrows   =  arrow_scale ./ norms
dV_arrows   = (dVdt_flat .* arrow_scale) ./ norms

p_field = quiver(T_flat, V_flat,
    quiver  = (dT_arrows, dV_arrows),
    xlabel  = "Time (ms)",
    ylabel  = "Membrane Voltage V (mV)",
    title   = "LIF Slope Field  (I = $(I_normal))",
    color   = :steelblue, alpha = 0.7, linewidth = 1.5,
    xlims   = (0, 6 * τ_lif), ylims = (-85, -28),
    legend  = :bottomright, label = "")

hline!([V_rest_lif]; linestyle = :dash, color = :gray,   lw = 2,
       label = "V_rest = $(V_rest_lif) mV")
hline!([V_thr_lif];  linestyle = :dash, color = :crimson, lw = 2,
       label = "V_threshold = $(V_thr_lif) mV")
display(p_field)
```

### 4.2 Simulated Voltage Trace

A direct DifferentialEquations.jl simulation reveals the sub-threshold charging and resets.
With `I = 1.52` the model period is ≈ 80 ms (model time), which maps to ≈ 800 ms
(physiological time) after the ×10 scaling applied in `simulate()`.

```{julia}
using DifferentialEquations

# ODE right-hand side
function lif_ode!(du, u, p, t)
    V = u[1]
    τ_p, V_rest_p, R_p, I_p = p
    du[1] = (-(V - V_rest_p) + R_p * I_p) / τ_p
end

# Spike-detection callback (upward threshold crossing)
spike_times_trace = Float64[]
spike_cond(u, t, integrator)  = u[1] - V_thr_lif
function spike_affect!(integrator)
    push!(spike_times_trace, integrator.t)
    integrator.u[1] = V_reset_lif
    length(spike_times_trace) >= 10 && terminate!(integrator)
end
cb = ContinuousCallback(spike_cond, spike_affect!, nothing,
                        rootfind = SciMLBase.RightRootFind)

prob = ODEProblem(lif_ode!, [V_rest_lif],
                 (0.0, 8000.0),
                 [τ_lif, V_rest_lif, R_lif, I_normal])
sol  = solve(prob, Tsit5(); callback = cb, dtmax = 0.1, saveat = 0.2)

p_trace = plot(sol.t, sol[1, :];
    xlabel = "Time (ms, model units)",
    ylabel = "Membrane Voltage (mV)",
    title  = "LIF Voltage Trace — I = $(I_normal)",
    color  = :steelblue, lw = 2, label = "V(t)")
hline!([V_thr_lif];  linestyle = :dash, color = :crimson, lw = 1.5,
       label = "V_threshold = $(V_thr_lif) mV")
hline!([V_rest_lif]; linestyle = :dash, color = :gray,   lw = 1.5,
       label = "V_rest = $(V_rest_lif) mV")

if length(spike_times_trace) >= 2
    ibis_model = diff(spike_times_trace)
    mean_T_model = round(mean(ibis_model); digits = 1)
    println("Spikes detected : $(length(spike_times_trace))")
    println("Mean IBI        : $(mean_T_model) ms")
    for st in spike_times_trace
        vline!([st]; linestyle = :dot, color = :orange, alpha = 0.8, label = "")
    end
end

# Each IBI is plotted at the midpoint between its two bounding spikes
p_ibi = plot(; xlabel = "Time (ms)",
               ylabel = "IBI (ms)",
               title  = "Model IBIs",
               ylims  = (0, nothing), legend = :topright)

if length(spike_times_trace) >= 2
    ibis_model   = diff(spike_times_trace)
    # Midpoint of each inter-spike interval
    t_ibi_mid    = (spike_times_trace[1:end-1] .+ spike_times_trace[2:end]) ./ 2
    ibis_ms      = ibis_model

    # Stem-style: vertical lines from zero up to each IBI value
    for (t_i, ibi_i) in zip(t_ibi_mid, ibis_ms)
        plot!(p_ibi, [t_i, t_i], [0.0, ibi_i];
              color = :teal, lw = 2, label = "")
    end
    scatter!(p_ibi, t_ibi_mid, ibis_ms;
             color = :teal, markersize = 6, label = "IBI (ms)")

    mean_ibi = round(mean(ibis_ms); digits = 1)
    hline!(p_ibi, [mean_ibi];
           linestyle = :dash, color = :orange, lw = 1.5,
           label = "Mean IBI = $(mean_ibi) ms")
    xlims!(p_ibi, (0-500, t_ibi_mid[end] + 1000))
end

plot(p_trace, p_ibi; layout = (2, 1), size = (1200, 800))
```

### 4.3 Rolling-Window Estimation of Input Current I(t)

We treat $I$ as **slowly varying** over the recording and estimate it on short, overlapping
windows of heartbeats. This converts the scalar fit into a time series $\hat{I}(t)$, making
visible how the autonomic drive to the heart changes over time.

**Window parameters**: 10-beat window · 2-beat stride.

#### Fitting the model to a single window

```{julia}
window_size = 24
stride      = 24
window1     = real_data[1:window_size]
lif_base = LIF(τ_lif, V_rest_lif, V_reset_lif, V_thr_lif, R_lif, I_normal)

# println("Fitting single window of $(window_size) beats with both methods…\n")
println("Fitting single window of $(window_size) beats with :analytical method…")
t_analytical = @elapsed result_analytical = fit(lif_base, window1; method = :analytical)
println("  $(round(t_analytical; digits = 3)) s   I = $(round(result_analytical.params.I; digits = 6))")
println()

println("Fitting single window of $(window_size) beats with :gradient method…")

t_grad  = @elapsed result_grad  = fit(lif_base, window1; method = :gradient)
println("  $(round(t_grad; digits = 3)) s   I = $(round(result_grad.params.I; digits = 6))")
println("  Converged : $(result_grad.diagnostics["converged"])  |  Iterations: $(result_grad.diagnostics["iterations"])")
println()

# t_bayes = @elapsed result_bayes = fit(lif_base, window1;
#     method = :bayesian, chains = 2, samples = 200)
# println("  :bayesian  →  $(round(t_bayes; digits = 2)) s   I ≈ $(round(result_bayes.params.I; digits = 6))")
# println()

# faster = t_grad < t_bayes ? ":gradient" : ":bayesian"
# println("▶ Faster method: $(faster) — will be used for the rolling fit")
```

#### Rolling fit over full recording

```{julia}
n_beats       = length(real_data)
window_starts = collect(1:stride:(n_beats - window_size + 1))
t_cumsum_ms   = cumsum(real_data)          # absolute beat timestamps in ms

I_series    = Vector{Float64}(undef, length(window_starts))
t_series    = Vector{Float64}(undef, length(window_starts))
rmse_series = Vector{Float64}(undef, length(window_starts))

println("Fitting $(length(window_starts)) windows (size=$(window_size), stride=$(stride))…")
t_rolling = @elapsed for (k, s) in enumerate(window_starts)
    w   = real_data[s : s + window_size - 1]
    res = fit(lif_base, w; method = :analytical)
    I_series[k] = res.params.I

    # Prediction RMSE: simulate with fitted I and compare to actual IBIs
    predicted       = simulate(lif_base, res.params, length(w))
    rmse_series[k]  = sqrt(mean((w .- predicted) .^ 2))

    # Window centre time: midpoint beat timestamp
    center_idx  = s + window_size ÷ 2 - 1
    t_series[k] = t_cumsum_ms[center_idx]
end
println("Done — $(length(I_series)) I estimates computed.")
println("  Elapsed time: $(round(t_rolling; digits=3)) s")

println("\nI(t) summary:")
println("  Mean  : $(round(mean(I_series);    digits = 6))")
println("  Std   : $(round(std(I_series);     digits = 6))")
println("  Min   : $(round(minimum(I_series); digits = 6))")
println("  Max   : $(round(maximum(I_series); digits = 6))")
println("\nRMSE summary (ms):")
println("  Mean  : $(round(mean(rmse_series);    digits = 3))")
println("  Std   : $(round(std(rmse_series);     digits = 3))")
println("  Min   : $(round(minimum(rmse_series); digits = 3))")
println("  Max   : $(round(maximum(rmse_series); digits = 3))")
```

```{julia}
t_sec         = t_series ./ 1000.0            # convert ms → s for the x-axis
t_real_sec    = cumsum(real_data) ./ 1000.0   # physiological timeline for raw IBIs
# xlim_range    = (0.0, t_real_sec[end])        # shared x-axis limits
xlim_range    = (2000.0, 3000.0)

# Convert RMSE (ms) to uncertainty in I-space via first-order approximation:
#   δI ≈ (I / mean_IBI) × RMSE_IBI   (IBI ∝ 1/I in the LIF model)
mean_ibi_global = mean(real_data)
ribbon_I = (I_series ./ mean_ibi_global) .* rmse_series .* 0.1 # Scale factor since current scales between 1.48 and 1.56, not 0 to 100

p_I = plot(t_sec, I_series;
    ribbon = ribbon_I,
    fillalpha = 0.25, fillcolor = :teal,
    xlabel = "", ylabel = "Input Current I",
    title  = "Continuous LIF Drive  I(t)  (window=$(window_size) beats · stride=$(stride))",
    xlims = xlim_range,
    lw = 1.5, color = :teal, label = "Î(t)")
hline!([1.52]; linestyle = :dash, color = :gray, lw = 1.5,
       label = "Default I = 1.52")

p_rmse = plot(t_sec, rmse_series;
    xlabel = "", ylabel = "RMSE (ms)",
    title  = "Per-window IBI Prediction Error",
    xlims = xlim_range,
    lw = 1.5, color = :coral, label = "RMSE(t)")
hline!([mean(rmse_series)]; linestyle = :dash, color = :gray, lw = 1.5,
       label = "Mean = $(round(mean(rmse_series); digits=1)) ms")

p_ibi = plot(t_real_sec, real_data;
    xlabel = "Time (s)", ylabel = "IBI (ms)",
    title  = "Raw IBI Signal",
    xlims = xlim_range,
    lw = 0.8, color = :steelblue, alpha = 0.7, label = "IBI(t)")
hline!([mean(real_data)]; linestyle = :dash, color = :gray, lw = 1.5,
       label = "Mean = $(round(mean(real_data); digits=1)) ms")

plot(p_I, p_rmse, p_ibi; layout = (3, 1), size = (900, 800), link = :x)
```

#### Point-to-point analytical I(t) — full recording

Rather than estimating a single $\hat{I}$ per window, the analytical inversion
$I_k = \Delta V \;/\; \bigl(R\,(1 - e^{-T_k/\tau})\bigr)$
gives an exact current value **for every beat** $k$.
`parameter_series(result, :I)` retrieves this full array from the fit result.

```{julia}
# Single analytical fit over the entire recording
result_full = fit(lif_base, real_data; method = :analytical)
xlim_range = (2000.0, 3000.0)

# Beat-by-beat I and its physiological timestamp
I_pointwise = parameter_series(result_full, :I)          # one value per beat
t_beats_sec = cumsum(real_data) ./ 1000.0                # beat timestamps (s)

println("Beat-by-beat I summary ($(length(I_pointwise)) beats):")
println("  Mean : $(round(mean(I_pointwise); digits=6))")
println("  Std  : $(round(std(I_pointwise);  digits=6))")
println("  Min  : $(round(minimum(I_pointwise); digits=6))")
println("  Max  : $(round(maximum(I_pointwise); digits=6))")

p_pt = plot(t_beats_sec, I_pointwise;
    xlabel  = "Time (s)", ylabel  = "Input Current I",
    title   = "Point-to-point Analytical I(t)  —  one value per beat",
    lw = 0.6, color = :teal, alpha = 0.7, label = "I_k (per beat)", xlims = xlim_range)
hline!([1.52]; linestyle = :dash, color = :gray, lw = 1.5,
       label = "Default I = 1.52")
hline!([mean(I_pointwise)];
    linestyle = :dot, color = :gray, lw = 1.5,
    label = "Mean = $(round(mean(I_pointwise); digits=4))")

# Overlay the windowed estimate for comparison
plot!(t_sec, I_series;
    lw = 2.0, color = :orange, label = "Windowed Î(t) (w=$(window_size))")

plot(p_pt, p_I, p_rmse, p_ibi; layout = (4, 1), size = (1200, 900), link = :x)
```

#### Concatenated Simulated Signal — Window-by-Window Reconstruction

Each of the $(length(window_starts)) rolling windows has a fitted $\hat{I}_k$.
We call `simulate()` per window to obtain `window_size` LIF IBIs, then concatenate
all windows into a single synthetic recording.  A separate ODE sweep builds the
corresponding membrane voltage trace for the first `seg_windows` windows so the
characteristic sawtooth charging-and-reset pattern is visible, with the threshold
current changing window-by-window.

```{julia}
# ── Build concatenated synthetic IBI series (one simulate() call per window) ─
t0_concat = time()
simulated_ibis_all = vcat([simulate(lif_base, (I = I_k,), window_size)
                           for I_k in I_series]...)
println("Simulated $(length(simulated_ibis_all)) IBIs from $(length(I_series)) windows  " *
        "($(round((time()-t0_concat); digits=2)) s)")

# ── Voltage trace for the first seg_windows windows ───────────────────────────
seg_windows = 20              # windows to trace (~480 beats)

# Helper: run LIF ODE for one window, return (t_vec, V_vec)
function lif_window_trace(I_k, n_beats, τ, V_rest, V_reset, V_thr, R)
    spikes_w = Float64[]

    function cond_w(u, t, int)
        u[1] - V_thr
    end
    function affect_w!(int)
        push!(spikes_w, int.t)
        int.u[1] = V_reset
        length(spikes_w) >= n_beats && terminate!(int)
    end
    cb_w = ContinuousCallback(cond_w, affect_w!, nothing;
                              rootfind = SciMLBase.RightRootFind)
    prob_w = ODEProblem(lif_ode!, [V_rest],
                        (0.0, 3000.0 * n_beats),
                        [τ, V_rest, R, I_k])
    sol_w  = solve(prob_w, Tsit5(); callback = cb_w, dtmax = 0.5, saveat = 0.5)
    return sol_w.t, sol_w[1, :]
end

V_trace = Float64[]
t_trace = Float64[]
t_global_ode = 0.0
for I_k in I_series[1:seg_windows]
    tw, Vw = lif_window_trace(I_k, window_size,
                              τ_lif, V_rest_lif, V_reset_lif, V_thr_lif, R_lif)
    append!(t_trace, tw .+ t_global_ode)
    append!(V_trace, Vw)
    t_global_ode += tw[end]
end
t_trace_sec = t_trace ./ 1000.0
println("Voltage trace: $(length(t_trace)) points over " *
        "$(round(t_global_ode / 1000; digits = 1)) s  ($(seg_windows) windows)")
```

```{julia}
# ── Align simulated and real timelines for comparison ─────────────────────────
n_compare       = min(length(simulated_ibis_all), length(real_data))

t_real_sec_full = cumsum(real_data[1:n_compare])          ./ 1000.0
# xlim_cmp        = (0.0, t_real_sec_full[end])
xlim_cmp        = (2000.0, 3000.0)

# Panel 1: Membrane voltage trace
p_vtrace = plot(t_trace_sec, V_trace;
    xlabel = "", ylabel = "V (mV)",
    title  = "LIF Voltage Trace — $(seg_windows) windows, window-by-window I",
    xlims  = (0.0, t_trace_sec[end]),
    lw = 0.5, color = :steelblue, alpha = 0.9, label = "V(t)")
hline!([V_thr_lif];  linestyle = :dash, color = :crimson, lw = 1.2,
       label = "V_thr = $(V_thr_lif) mV")
hline!([V_rest_lif]; linestyle = :dash, color = :gray,    lw = 1.2,
       label = "V_rest = $(V_rest_lif) mV")

# Panel 2: Simulated IBIs with per-window RMSE ribbon
rmse_sim = sqrt(mean((simulated_ibis_all[1:n_compare] .- real_data[1:n_compare]) .^ 2))
# Per-beat RMSE: each window of window_size beats gets its own rmse_series[k]
ribbon_beat = repeat(rmse_series, inner = window_size)[1:n_compare]

p_sim = plot(t_sim_sec_full, simulated_ibis_all[1:n_compare];
    ribbon = ribbon_beat,
    fillalpha = 0.25, fillcolor = :teal,
    xlabel = "", ylabel = "IBI (ms)",
    title  = "Simulated IBIs — $(length(I_series)) windows concatenated  |  RMSE = $(round(rmse_sim; digits = 2)) ms",
    xlims  = xlim_cmp,
    lw = 0.7, color = :teal, alpha = 0.75, label = "Simulated IBI")
mean_sim = mean(simulated_ibis_all[1:n_compare])
hline!([mean_sim];
    linestyle = :dash, color = :gray, lw = 1.5,
    label = "Mean = $(round(mean_sim; digits = 1)) ms")

# Panel 3: Real IBIs
p_real_cmp = plot(t_real_sec_full, real_data[1:n_compare];
    xlabel = "Time (s)", ylabel = "IBI (ms)",
    title  = "Real IBIs  |  RMSE = $(round(rmse_sim; digits = 2)) ms",
    xlims  = xlim_cmp,
    lw = 0.7, color = :steelblue, alpha = 0.7, label = "Real IBI")
hline!([mean(real_data[1:n_compare])];
    linestyle = :dash, color = :gray, lw = 1.5,
    label = "Mean = $(round(mean(real_data[1:n_compare]); digits = 1)) ms")

plot(p_vtrace, p_sim, p_real_cmp; layout = (3, 1), size = (1200, 900), link = :x)
```

## Part 5: Normative Comparison — Distribution-Aware Analysis

This section evaluates our example recording against two curated healthy-population databases
from PhysioNet: the **Normal Sinus Rhythm Database (NSRDB)** and the **Normal Sinus Rhythm
RR Interval Database (NSR2DB)**.

HeartRateLab ships fitted normative **prior distributions** for every HRV feature — not just
Normal, but also Gamma, LogNormal, and Beta families chosen per-feature by goodness-of-fit.
The σ-band overlays, percentile scores, and z-equivalent values shown below are all
**distribution-aware**: they use quantile intervals from the fitted prior rather than
assuming symmetry.

### 5.1 Setup: Load Normative Datasets & Priors

```{julia}
using CSV, Printf, Distributions

# ── Window parameters (must match the pre-computed CSVs) ──────────────────────
norm_window_size = 360   # beats per window
norm_stride      = 120   # beat stride between windows

# ── Features of interest ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
norm_features    = ["rmssd", "mean", "sdnn", "lf", "hf", "sd1", "sd2"]
pairplot_features = ["rmssd", "sdnn", "lf", "hf", "sd1", "sd2"]

feat_labels = Dict(
    "rmssd" => "RMSSD (ms)",
    "mean"  => "Mean IBI (ms)",
    "sdnn"  => "SDNN (ms)",
    "lf"    => "LF Power (ms²)",
    "hf"    => "HF Power (ms²)",
    "sd1"   => "SD1 (ms)",
    "sd2"   => "SD2 (ms)",
)

# ── Helper: find a file relative to project root (works from docs/ or root) ──
function _find(rel::String)
    for prefix in ["", "../"]
        p = prefix * rel
        isfile(p) && return p
    end
    error("Cannot find $rel")
end

# ── Load windowed features for NSRDB and NSR2DB ─────────────────────────────
wf_csv = "windowed_w$(norm_window_size)_s$(norm_stride)_features.csv"

nsrdb_wf = CSV.read(_find("test/testdata/nsrdb/$wf_csv"), DataFrame)
nsr2db_wf = CSV.read(_find("test/testdata/nsr2db/$wf_csv"), DataFrame)

println("NSRDB:  $(nrow(nsrdb_wf)) windows from $(length(unique(nsrdb_wf.participant_id))) participants")
println("NSR2DB: $(nrow(nsr2db_wf)) windows from $(length(unique(nsr2db_wf.participant_id))) participants")

# ── Combine into "All Normal" reference ──────────────────────────────────────
all_normal_wf = vcat(nsrdb_wf, nsr2db_wf; cols=:intersect)
println("Combined normal: $(nrow(all_normal_wf)) windows")

# ── Window the individual recording with matching parameters ─────────────────
indiv_wf = windowed_feature_set(real_data;
    window_size=norm_window_size, stride=norm_stride, features=norm_features)
println("Individual: $(nrow(indiv_wf)) windows")
```

```{julia}
# ── Verify normative priors are loaded ────────────────────────────────────────
n_priors = length(prior_registry)
println("Loaded $n_priors fitted normative priors")
for feat in norm_features
    d = normative_prior(feat)
    if d !== nothing
        println("  $feat ~ $(typeof(d).name.name)($(join(round.(collect(params(d)); digits=3), ", ")))")
    else
        println("  $feat — no prior available")
    end
end
```

### 5.2 Participant-Level Feature Histograms

```{julia}
nsrdb_pf  = CSV.read(_find("test/testdata/nsrdb/participant_features.csv"), DataFrame)
nsr2db_pf = CSV.read(_find("test/testdata/nsr2db/participant_features.csv"), DataFrame)
all_normal_pf = vcat(nsrdb_pf, nsr2db_pf; cols=:intersect)

# Extract individual's whole-recording features
indiv_pf = extract_feature_set(real_data; features=norm_features)

println("$(nrow(nsrdb_pf)) NSRDB + $(nrow(nsr2db_pf)) NSR2DB = $(nrow(all_normal_pf)) healthy participants")
```

```{julia}
# ── Histograms with individual vertical line & fitted prior PDF ──────────────
hist_plots = map(norm_features) do feat
    vals = filter(!isnan, all_normal_pf[!, feat])
    indiv_val = indiv_pf[!, feat][1]

    h = histogram(vals;
        title     = feat_labels[feat],
        xlabel    = feat_labels[feat],
        ylabel    = "Density",
        normalize = :pdf,
        alpha     = 0.55,
        color     = :steelblue,
        label     = "Healthy (n=$(length(vals)))",
        legend    = :topright,
    )

    # Overlay fitted prior PDF if available
    d = normative_prior(feat)
    if d !== nothing
        x_range = range(quantile(d, 0.005), quantile(d, 0.995); length=200)
        plot!(x_range, pdf.(d, x_range);
            color=:grey30, lw=2, ls=:dash, alpha=0.8,
            label="Prior: $(typeof(d).name.name)")
    end

    vline!([indiv_val];
        color=:crimson, lw=2.5, linestyle=:dash, label="Individual")
    h
end

plot(hist_plots...; layout=(4, 2), size=(1100, 900),
     plot_title="Participant-Level HRV Features — Healthy Population vs Individual")
```

### 5.3 Normative KDE Comparison (Distribution-Aware)

The `plot_normative_kde_comparison` function draws KDE curves for each dataset with
**distribution-aware σ-band overlays** derived from the fitted prior.  For skewed features
(e.g. HF power ~ Gamma, LF/HF ratio ~ LogNormal) the bands use quantile intervals rather
than symmetric mean ± σ, correctly representing the true dispersion.

```{julia}
# ── Build the datasets dict for the normative KDE comparison ─────────────────
norm_datasets = Dict(
    "NSRDB"      => nsrdb_wf,
    "NSR2DB"     => nsr2db_wf,
    "Individual" => indiv_wf,
)

plot_normative_kde_comparison(
    norm_datasets, norm_features;
    reference_key = "NSRDB",
    feat_labels   = feat_labels,
    ncols         = 3,
    title         = "Normative KDE Comparison — $(norm_window_size)-beat windows",
)
```

### 5.4 Distribution-Aware Normative Scoring

Rather than assuming all features follow a Normal distribution, we use the **fitted prior**
to compute each individual's percentile and an equivalent z-score:

1. Compute the **median** of the individual's windowed feature values (session-length independent).
2. Evaluate the **CDF** of the fitted prior at that median → percentile.
3. Convert the percentile to a **z-equivalent** via the inverse Normal CDF.

This approach correctly handles skewed distributions (Gamma for power features, Beta for
proportions, LogNormal for ratios).

```{julia}
# ── Distribution-aware z-scoring ─────────────────────────────────────────────
zscore_rows = map(norm_features) do feat
    indiv_vals = filter(!isnan, indiv_wf[!, feat])
    indiv_med  = median(indiv_vals)

    d = normative_prior(feat)
    if d !== nothing
        pct       = cdf(d, indiv_med)
        pct_clamp = clamp(pct, 1e-8, 1.0 - 1e-8)
        z_eq      = quantile(Normal(), pct_clamp)
        family    = string(typeof(d).name.name)
        loc       = mean(d)
        (feature=feat, family=family, location=round(loc; digits=2),
         indiv_median=round(indiv_med; digits=2),
         percentile=round(pct; digits=4), z_equiv=round(z_eq; digits=3),
         n_windows=length(indiv_vals))
    else
        # Fallback: empirical Normal from combined reference
        ref_vals = filter(!isnan, all_normal_wf[!, feat])
        μ = mean(ref_vals); σ = std(ref_vals)
        z = (indiv_med - μ) / σ
        pct = cdf(Normal(μ, σ), indiv_med)
        (feature=feat, family="Normal*", location=round(μ; digits=2),
         indiv_median=round(indiv_med; digits=2),
         percentile=round(pct; digits=4), z_equiv=round(z; digits=3),
         n_windows=length(indiv_vals))
    end
end

zscore_df = DataFrame(zscore_rows)
println("─"^85)
println("  Feature │  Family     │  Location  │  Indiv med │  Percentile │  z-equiv")
println("─"^85)
for r in eachrow(zscore_df)
    @printf("  %-7s │  %-9s  │  %8.2f  │  %8.2f  │   %6.2f%%   │  %+.3f\n",
            r.feature, r.family, r.location, r.indiv_median,
            r.percentile * 100, r.z_equiv)
end
println("─"^85)
println("  Scoring uses $(norm_window_size)-beat windows ($(zscore_df.n_windows[1]) individual windows)")
```

```{julia}
# ── Summary interpretation ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
println("\n  Normative Scoring Summary")
println("="^72)
println("  Feature │  z-equiv │  Interpretation")
println("─"^72)
for r in eachrow(zscore_df)
    z = abs(r.z_equiv)
    interp = if z <= 1.0
        "Within ±1σ  — typical"
    elseif z <= 2.0
        "Within ±2σ  — slightly atypical"
    elseif z <= 3.0
        "Within ±3σ  — notably atypical"
    else
        "Beyond  ±3σ — rare (<0.3%)"
    end
    @printf("  %-7s │  %+.3f   │  %s\n", r.feature, r.z_equiv, interp)
end
println("="^72)
```

The correlogram reveals the linear relationships between HRV features across the
combined normative population.  Strong correlations (red = positive, blue = negative)
indicate redundant features or known physiological couplings (e.g. RMSSD ↔ SD1).

```{julia}

    title="Feature Correlations — Healthy Population ($(nrow(all_normal_wf)) windows)")
```
